findings.reason: The protected sources use the conventional slow/fast midpoint scan, reverse only the comparison suffix, compare mirrored values with two forward walks, and reverse the suffix again before returning. The result is clear, O(n)-time, O(1)-auxiliary-space, and preserves the input topology, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local function and Accepted native method have identical midpoint, reversal, comparison, saved-result, and restoration logic. The app-local ListNode class is the required standalone equivalent of LeetCode's injected model.

The former benchmark used node values through 16 despite the source maximum of 9. Legal 16/64/256-node mirrored-digit lists now exercise full comparison and restoration. The protected source passes at -0.01 relative exponent; a correct implementation that repeatedly walks to each mirrored position passes every output and fails only scaling at +1.00 with a 25.51x largest runtime ratio.

The prior Approach called restoration an optional alternative even though the protected source always performs it. The document now explains the second reversal and implicit reconnection exactly, and distinguishes one-node, even-length, and odd-length behavior.
